verses.1: She directed their works in the hands of the holy prophet.
verses.2: They made a path through desolate areas, which were uninhabited, and set up their homes in remote places.
verses.3: They stood firm against the enemy, and vindicated themselves from their adversaries.
verses.4: They thirsted, and they called upon you, and water was given them out of the deepest rock, and respite from thirst out of the hard stone.
verses.5: For through water, their enemies had been punished, by the corruption of their drinking water; and so, among them, when the sons of Israel lacked the abundance they would have had, their enemies rejoiced;
verses.6: yet through water, when they were in need, it turned out well for them.
verses.7: For instead of a fountain, even everlasting in flow, you gave human blood to the unjust,
verses.8: and while they would be crushed into disgrace because of the murdering of infants, you unexpectedly gave your own abundant water,
verses.9: revealing through the thirst, which occurred at that time, how you would exalt your own and would kill their adversaries.
verses.10: For when they were being tested, and even when receiving merciful correction, they knew in what way, when your wrath judged the impious, they would suffer torments.
verses.11: For these, advising like a father, you approved; but the others, interrogating like a severe king, you condemned.
verses.12: For whether absent or present, they were tortured alike.
verses.13: For they had received double: weariness and groaning in the remembrance of things past.
verses.14: For when they paid attention to their punishments, to attend to their own benefit, they called to mind the Lord, admiring the end result.
verses.15: For though they showed scorn by throwing out distorted statements, in the end they were amazed at the result, but this is not the same as thirsting for justice.
verses.16: For according to the thinking of their irrational iniquity, because some, going astray, were worshiping mute serpents and worthless beasts, you sent upon them a multitude of mute beasts for vengeance,
verses.17: so that they might know that by whatever things a man sins, by the same also is he tormented.
verses.18: For it was not impossible for your all-powerful hand, which created the world from unknown material, to send forth upon them a multitude of bears, or fierce lions,
verses.19: or, in anger, beasts of a new kind, massive and strange, either breathing out a fiery vapor, or sending forth an odorous smoke, or shooting horrible sparks from their eyes;
verses.20: whereby, not only wounds would be able to destroy them, but also the very sight would kill them through fear.
verses.21: Yet, even without these, they could have been killed with one breath, suffering persecution of their own making and being scattered by your spirit of virtue; but you have ordered all things in size and number and weight.
verses.22: Though many are strong, you alone always overcome. And who will withstand the strength of your arm?
verses.23: For, like a tiny grain on a scale, just so is the world before you, and like a drop of dew before dawn, which descends upon the earth.
verses.24: But you are merciful to all, because you can do all, and you dismiss the sins of man because of repentance.
verses.25: For you love all things that are, and you hate nothing of the things you have made; for you would not have created or established anything that you hated.
verses.26: For how could anything endure, except by your will? Or what, having been called by you not to exist, would be preserved?
verses.27: Yet you spare all things, because they are yours, O Lord, who loves souls. [ Wisdom 12 ]
